import Mathlib

open scoped BigOperators

namespace CoefficientCertificate

abbrev BinaryMatrix (m n : ℕ) := Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) (ZMod 2)

def rowParity {m n : ℕ} (P : BinaryMatrix m n) (i : Fin m) : ZMod 2 :=
  ∑ j, P i j

def colParity {m n : ℕ} (P : BinaryMatrix m n) (j : Fin n) : ZMod 2 :=
  ∑ i, P i j

def totalParity {m n : ℕ} (P : BinaryMatrix m n) : ZMod 2 :=
  ∑ i, ∑ j, P i j

lemma binary_ne_zero_eq_one (x : ZMod 2) (h : x ≠ 0) : x = 1 := by
  fin_cases x
  · exact (h rfl).elim
  · rfl

lemma binary_mul_eq_one (x y : ZMod 2) (h : x * y = 1) :
    x = 1 ∧ y = 1 := by
  have hx : x ≠ 0 := by
    intro hx
    rw [hx, zero_mul] at h
    exact zero_ne_one h
  have hy : y ≠ 0 := by
    intro hy
    rw [hy, mul_zero] at h
    exact zero_ne_one h
  exact ⟨binary_ne_zero_eq_one x hx, binary_ne_zero_eq_one y hy⟩

lemma exists_one {n : ℕ} (p : Fin n → ZMod 2) (hp : p ≠ 0) :
    ∃ i, p i = 1 := by
  classical
  by_contra h
  apply hp
  funext i
  by_contra hi
  exact h ⟨i, binary_ne_zero_eq_one (p i) hi⟩

theorem rectangle_row_parity {m n : ℕ}
    (p : Fin m → ZMod 2) (h : Fin n → ZMod 2) :
    rowParity (Matrix.vecMulVec p h) = fun i => p i * ∑ j, h j := by
  funext i
  simp [rowParity, Matrix.vecMulVec, Finset.mul_sum]

theorem rectangle_col_parity {m n : ℕ}
    (p : Fin m → ZMod 2) (h : Fin n → ZMod 2) :
    colParity (Matrix.vecMulVec p h) = fun j => (∑ i, p i) * h j := by
  funext j
  simp [colParity, Matrix.vecMulVec, Finset.sum_mul]

theorem rectangle_total_parity {m n : ℕ}
    (p : Fin m → ZMod 2) (h : Fin n → ZMod 2) :
    totalParity (Matrix.vecMulVec p h) = (∑ i, p i) * ∑ j, h j := by
  change (∑ i, ∑ j, p i * h j) = (∑ i, p i) * ∑ j, h j
  rw [Finset.sum_mul]
  simp only [Finset.mul_sum]

theorem odd_rectangle_parities {m n : ℕ}
    (p : Fin m → ZMod 2) (h : Fin n → ZMod 2)
    (hodd : totalParity (Matrix.vecMulVec p h) = 1) :
    (∑ i, p i) = 1 ∧ (∑ j, h j) = 1 ∧
      rowParity (Matrix.vecMulVec p h) = p ∧
      colParity (Matrix.vecMulVec p h) = h := by
  rw [rectangle_total_parity] at hodd
  obtain ⟨hp, hh⟩ := binary_mul_eq_one _ _ hodd
  refine ⟨hp, hh, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [rectangle_row_parity, hh]
    simp
  · rw [rectangle_col_parity, hp]
    simp

theorem rectangle_unique {m n : ℕ}
    (p q : Fin m → ZMod 2) (h k : Fin n → ZMod 2)
    (hp : p ≠ 0) (hh : h ≠ 0)
    (heq : Matrix.vecMulVec p h = Matrix.vecMulVec q k) :
    p = q ∧ h = k := by
  obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := exists_one p hp
  obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := exists_one h hh
  have hpivot : q i * k j = 1 := by
    have ht := congrFun (congrFun heq i) j
    simpa [Matrix.vecMulVec, hi, hj] using ht.symm
  obtain ⟨hqi, hkj⟩ := binary_mul_eq_one _ _ hpivot
  constructor
  · funext r
    have ht := congrFun (congrFun heq r) j
    simpa [Matrix.vecMulVec, hj, hkj] using ht
  · funext c
    have ht := congrFun (congrFun heq i) c
    simpa [Matrix.vecMulVec, hi, hqi] using ht

def rowSupported {m n : ℕ} (P : BinaryMatrix m n) (i : Fin m) : Prop :=
  ∀ r, r ≠ i → ∀ j, P r j = 0

def colSupported {m n : ℕ} (P : BinaryMatrix m n) (j : Fin n) : Prop :=
  ∀ c, c ≠ j → ∀ i, P i c = 0

instance {m n : ℕ} (P : BinaryMatrix m n) (i : Fin m) :
    Decidable (rowSupported P i) := by
  unfold rowSupported
  infer_instance

instance {m n : ℕ} (P : BinaryMatrix m n) (j : Fin n) :
    Decidable (colSupported P j) := by
  unfold colSupported
  infer_instance

theorem row_supported_rank_le_one {m n : ℕ}
    (P : BinaryMatrix m n) (i : Fin m) (hs : rowSupported P i) :
    P.rank ≤ 1 := by
  classical
  have heq : P = Matrix.vecMulVec (Pi.single i (1 : ZMod 2)) (P i) := by
    ext r j
    by_cases hr : r = i
    · subst r
      simp [Matrix.vecMulVec]
    · simp [Matrix.vecMulVec, Pi.single_apply, hr, hs r hr j]
  rw [heq]
  exact Matrix.rank_vecMulVec_le _ _

theorem col_supported_rank_le_one {m n : ℕ}
    (P : BinaryMatrix m n) (j : Fin n) (hs : colSupported P j) :
    P.rank ≤ 1 := by
  have ht : rowSupported P.transpose j := hs
  simpa only [Matrix.rank_transpose] using row_supported_rank_le_one P.transpose j ht

noncomputable def lowRankPart {m n : ℕ}
    (c : BinaryMatrix m n → ℝ) (P : BinaryMatrix m n) : ℝ :=
  if P.rank ≤ 1 then c P else 0

theorem high_rank_row_coefficient_zero {m n : ℕ}
    (c : BinaryMatrix m n → ℝ) (a : ℝ) (g : (Fin n → ZMod 2) → ℝ)
    (i : Fin m)
    (hproj : ∀ P, (if rowParity P = Pi.single i 1 then c P else 0) =
      if rowSupported P i then a * g (P i) else 0)
    (P : BinaryMatrix m n) (hrank : 1 < P.rank)
    (hpar : rowParity P = Pi.single i 1) :
    c P = 0 := by
  classical
  have hs : ¬rowSupported P i := by
    intro hs
    exact (not_le_of_gt hrank) (row_supported_rank_le_one P i hs)
  simpa [hpar, hs] using hproj P

theorem row_projection_survives {m n : ℕ}
    (c : BinaryMatrix m n → ℝ) (a : ℝ) (g : (Fin n → ZMod 2) → ℝ)
    (i : Fin m)
    (hproj : ∀ P, (if rowParity P = Pi.single i 1 then c P else 0) =
      if rowSupported P i then a * g (P i) else 0) :
    ∀ P, (if rowParity P = Pi.single i 1 then lowRankPart c P else 0) =
      if rowSupported P i then a * g (P i) else 0 := by
  classical
  intro P
  by_cases hrank : P.rank ≤ 1
  · simpa [lowRankPart, hrank] using hproj P
  · have hs : ¬rowSupported P i := fun hs =>
      hrank (row_supported_rank_le_one P i hs)
    simp [lowRankPart, hrank, hs]

theorem col_projection_survives {m n : ℕ}
    (c : BinaryMatrix m n → ℝ) (b : ℝ) (f : (Fin m → ZMod 2) → ℝ)
    (j : Fin n)
    (hproj : ∀ P, (if colParity P = Pi.single j 1 then c P else 0) =
      if colSupported P j then b * f (fun i => P i j) else 0) :
    ∀ P, (if colParity P = Pi.single j 1 then lowRankPart c P else 0) =
      if colSupported P j then b * f (fun i => P i j) else 0 := by
  classical
  intro P
  by_cases hrank : P.rank ≤ 1
  · simpa [lowRankPart, hrank] using hproj P
  · have hs : ¬colSupported P j := fun hs =>
      hrank (col_supported_rank_le_one P j hs)
    simp [lowRankPart, hrank, hs]

def parityMass (r : ℚ) : ℕ → ℚ × ℚ
  | 0 => (1, 0)
  | n + 1 =>
      let p := parityMass r n
      (p.1 + r * p.2, p.2 + r * p.1)

theorem parity_mass_sum (r : ℚ) (n : ℕ) :
    (parityMass r n).1 + (parityMass r n).2 = (1 + r) ^ n := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp [parityMass]
  | succ n ih =>
      simp only [parityMass, pow_succ]
      calc
        _ = ((parityMass r n).1 + (parityMass r n).2) * (1 + r) := by ring
        _ = _ := by rw [ih]

theorem parity_mass_sub (r : ℚ) (n : ℕ) :
    (parityMass r n).1 - (parityMass r n).2 = (1 - r) ^ n := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp [parityMass]
  | succ n ih =>
      simp only [parityMass, pow_succ]
      calc
        _ = ((parityMass r n).1 - (parityMass r n).2) * (1 - r) := by ring
        _ = _ := by rw [ih]

theorem odd_mass_closed (r : ℚ) (n : ℕ) :
    (parityMass r n).2 = ((1 + r) ^ n - (1 - r) ^ n) / 2 := by
  linarith [parity_mass_sum r n, parity_mass_sub r n]

theorem tail_log_exponent (k l t : ℝ) (ht : 0 ≤ t)
    (hk : 2 * t ≤ k) (hl : 2 * t ≤ l) :
    (k + l) * t ≤ k * l := by
  have hk0 : 0 ≤ k := by linarith
  have hl0 : 0 ≤ l := by linarith
  nlinarith [mul_nonneg hk0 (sub_nonneg.mpr hl),
    mul_nonneg hl0 (sub_nonneg.mpr hk)]

theorem tail_geometric_exponent (k l : ℝ) (hk : 4 ≤ k) (hl : 4 ≤ l) :
    k + l ≤ k * l / 2 := by
  nlinarith [mul_nonneg (sub_nonneg.mpr hk) (sub_nonneg.mpr hl)]

theorem quantitative_margin (d A B K epsilon W : ℝ)
    (hd : 4 ≤ d)
    (hA : 80 * (d * (d + 1) ^ 2) ≤ A)
    (hB : 80 * (d * (d + 1) ^ 2) ≤ B)
    (hmixed : A * B / 2 ≤ 4 * (d * (d + 1)) * (A + B) +
      5 * K * (d * (d + 1)) * (d * (d + 1) ^ 2))
    (hK : K ≤ 8 + epsilon * W) :
    640 * d + 504 ≤ epsilon * W := by
  let D := d * (d + 1)
  let L := d * (d + 1) ^ 2
  have hD : 0 < D := by dsimp [D]; positivity
  have hL : 0 < L := by dsimp [L]; positivity
  have hc : 0 ≤ 40 * L - 4 * D := by
    dsimp [L, D]
    have hd0 : 0 ≤ d := by linarith
    nlinarith [sq_nonneg d]
  have hres : 0 ≤ (40 * L - 4 * D) * ((A - 80 * L) + (B - 80 * L)) +
      (A - 80 * L) * (B - 80 * L) / 2 := by
    have hAa : 0 ≤ A - 80 * L := sub_nonneg.mpr hA
    have hBb : 0 ≤ B - 80 * L := sub_nonneg.mpr hB
    positivity
  have hid : A * B / 2 - 4 * D * (A + B) -
      (640 * d + 512) * (5 * D * L) =
      (40 * L - 4 * D) * ((A - 80 * L) + (B - 80 * L)) +
        (A - 80 * L) * (B - 80 * L) / 2 := by
    dsimp [D, L]
    ring
  have hmult : (640 * d + 512) * (5 * D * L) ≤ K * (5 * D * L) := by
    change A * B / 2 ≤ 4 * D * (A + B) + 5 * K * D * L at hmixed
    nlinarith [hid, hres]
  have hfactor : 0 < 5 * D * L := by positivity
  have hbound : 640 * d + 512 ≤ K := le_of_mul_le_mul_right hmult hfactor
  linarith

theorem coefficient_from_mass (N : ℕ) (epsilon W : ℝ)
    (he : 0 ≤ epsilon) (hW : W ≤ (3 / 2 : ℝ) ^ N)
    (hm : 1 ≤ epsilon * W) :
    (2 / 3 : ℝ) ^ N ≤ epsilon := by
  have hp : 0 < (3 / 2 : ℝ) ^ N := by positivity
  have hprod : 1 ≤ epsilon * (3 / 2 : ℝ) ^ N :=
    hm.trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hW he)
  have hinv : (2 / 3 : ℝ) ^ N * (3 / 2 : ℝ) ^ N = 1 := by
    rw [← mul_pow]
    norm_num
  have hcompare : (2 / 3 : ℝ) ^ N * (3 / 2 : ℝ) ^ N ≤
      epsilon * (3 / 2 : ℝ) ^ N := by
    simpa [hinv] using hprod
  exact le_of_mul_le_mul_right hcompare hp

end CoefficientCertificate

# Statement fidelity: scalar coefficient finite core

The source is `Main.lean`, namespace `CoefficientCertificate`, compiled with
Lean 4.31.0 and the host's built Mathlib. It supports ledger claim
`L_COEFF_FORMAL_CORE`. It does **not** encode the entire scalar coefficient
theorem or the Banach-space theorem. No declaration assumes the scalar
nonvanishing conclusion or an explicit coefficient lower bound.

## Objects and quantifiers

`BinaryMatrix m n` is `Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) (ZMod 2)` for arbitrary natural
row and column counts, including zero. `Matrix.rank` is rank over `ZMod 2`,
not over the rationals or the reals. `rowParity`, `colParity`, and
`totalParity` are sums in `ZMod 2`, hence parities, not integer weights.

`rectangle_row_parity`, `rectangle_col_parity`, and
`rectangle_total_parity` compute these sums for an arbitrary outer product
`p h^t`. `odd_rectangle_parities` assumes total parity one and proves both
factor sums are one and the row/column parity vectors are precisely `p,h`.
`rectangle_unique` assumes both original factor vectors are nonzero and
equality with another outer product, and proves equality of both factors.
The converse classification of every nonzero rank-one matrix as an outer
product is proved in the report, not formalized here.

`rowSupported P i` means every entry outside row `i` is zero;
`colSupported P j` is the analogous column assertion. The two
`*_supported_rank_le_one` declarations prove the corresponding actual
matrix-rank bounds.

## Exact coefficient-level projections

`c` is an arbitrary real-valued function of a binary matrix, interpreted in
the application as its uniform Fourier coefficient. `lowRankPart c P`
keeps `c P` when binary rank is at most one, and is zero otherwise.

`high_rank_row_coefficient_zero` assumes the **coefficient-level** row
projection identity for every index, binary rank greater than one, and row
parity equal to the selected unit vector. It proves that coefficient is
zero. The hypothesis says that selecting coefficients of that row parity
equals the row-supported coefficients of `a*g`; it is not a bound or a
nonvanishing assumption.

`row_projection_survives` and `col_projection_survives` assume the
corresponding original coefficient-level identity for all binary indices.
For arbitrary real `a,b` and arbitrary real coefficient arrays `g,f`, they
prove that the same identity holds for `lowRankPart c`.
The identification of these hypotheses with the manuscript's function
identities uses finite Fourier character orthogonality, which is proved
in the report and checked on small complete cubes by `verify.py`, not
formalized in Lean. In the application oddness ensures that the supported
row/column coefficient identities have exactly the stated form. No
sup-norm bound for the rank projection is assumed or proved.

## Weighted parity mass and tail exponents

`parityMass r n` is a pair of rational numbers defined by the exact even/odd
weighted-mass recurrence, starting with `(1,0)`. `parity_mass_sum`,
`parity_mass_sub`, and `odd_mass_closed` prove its closed formula for every
rational `r` and natural `n`. The combinatorial identification of this
recurrence with the sum of `r^|P|` over all odd binary matrices is explained
in the report; the formal theorem is about the recurrence itself.

`tail_log_exponent` is an inequality for real `k,l,t` with `t>=0` and
`k,l>=2t`; it proves `(k+l)t<=kl`. `tail_geometric_exponent` assumes real
`k,l>=4` and proves `k+l<=kl/2`. The logarithm comparison, Parseval,
probability expectation, and geometric summation are not formalized.

## Final margin and conversion

`quantitative_margin` quantifies over real `d,A,B,K,epsilon,W`. Its
hypotheses are `d>=4`, `A,B>=80d(d+1)^2`, the mixed-derivative upper
inequality

\[
 AB/2 \le 4d(d+1)(A+B)+5K\,d(d+1)\,d(d+1)^2,
\]

and `K<=8+epsilon*W`. It proves
`epsilon*W>=640d+504` by an exact nonnegative polynomial identity.
It does not assume positivity of `epsilon` or `W`, because that is
unnecessary for this algebraic implication. The existence of `H0` and
its Chebyshev/mixed-derivative estimates establishing these premises are
proved in prose, not discharged by this formal theorem.

`coefficient_from_mass` assumes a natural `N`, real `epsilon>=0`,
`W<=(3/2)^N`, and `epsilon*W>=1`. It proves
`epsilon>=(2/3)^N`. In the application
`N=m^2`, the odd-mass formula provides the mass bound and
`quantitative_margin` provides a strictly stronger lower bound on
`epsilon*W`.

The scalar theorem has no unproved external mathematical assumption.
Its remaining **non-formalized proof obligations** are the stated finite
Fourier translation, rank-one existence, Parseval/Cauchy--Schwarz,
noise expectation, tail summation, and elementary Chebyshev integral
argument. The full scalar claim is supported by a written proof and
exact replay, not labelled as a kernel-closed theorem.
